title: Load Testing LLM APIs — Why k6 and Locust Lie

questions.question: What prompt distribution does make_uniform_workload create?
options: Gaussian prompt lengths with 80 random prefixes
A mixture of 50–8,000-token prompts
500 requests with a 2,000-token prompt and one shared prefix
One unique prefix for every request
questions.explanation: The uniform fixture returns Request(2000, "single_prefix") for every one of its n requests.

questions.question: What TTFT does simulate assign to the first request for a previously unseen prefix?
options: 80 ms
800 ms
15 ms
0 ms
questions.explanation: A prefix miss uses PREFIX_CACHE_MISS_TTFT_MS=800; later hits use the 80 ms constant.

questions.question: How does make_realistic_workload choose its prefix IDs?
options: It chooses from prefix_0 through prefix_79
It always uses single_prefix
It hashes each prompt into a unique ID
It uses only the concurrency value
questions.explanation: The realistic fixture builds 80 prefixes and chooses rng.choice(prefixes), while prompt length comes from a clipped Gaussian.

questions.question: What happens to repeated requests after their prefix is inserted into cache?
options: They are rejected as duplicates
They receive the 80 ms cache-hit TTFT
They are counted as 800 ms misses forever
They change the prefix hash to a new value
questions.explanation: simulate adds an unseen prefix to cache and then assigns PREFIX_CACHE_HIT_TTFT_MS=80 to subsequent requests carrying it.

questions.question: Which percentile does the simulator read at index int(0.99 * len(samples)) - 1?
options: The arithmetic mean
questions.explanation: After sorting ttft_samples, that index is the reported P99; it is intentionally distinct from the mean and median fields.

questions.question: Why can the uniform benchmark make an endpoint look faster than realistic traffic?
options: It disables all TTFT measurement
It uses more unique prefixes and fewer cache hits
It sends no requests at concurrency 200
One shared prefix creates many cache hits and hides prefix diversity
questions.explanation: The uniform fixture's single_prefix quickly becomes a hit for nearly every request, whereas realistic traffic pays misses for many distinct prefixes.
